title: Personal Financial Literacy: Accounts, Credit, College and Careers
seo_title: Grade 6 Personal Financial Literacy Worksheets: Credit, Check Registers and College (TEKS 6.14, STAAR)
standard_text: 6.14A compare the features and costs of a checking account and a debit card offered by different local financial institutions; 6.14B distinguish between debit cards and credit cards; 6.14C balance a check register that includes deposits, withdrawals, and transfers; 6.14D explain why it is important to establish a positive credit history; 6.14E describe the information in a credit report and how long it is retained; 6.14F describe the value of credit reports to borrowers and to lenders; 6.14G explain various methods to pay for college, including through savings, grants, scholarships, student loans, and work-study; 6.14H compare the annual salary of several occupations requiring various levels of post-secondary education or vocational training and calculate the effects of the different annual salaries on lifetime income
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 personal financial literacy worksheets for Texas TEKS 6.14: checking accounts, debit and credit cards, check registers, credit reports, paying for college and lifetime income. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Debit spends your money; credit borrows it.
key_sub: Register: add deposits, subtract payments. Good credit means lower interest.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A checking account and a debit card use your own money. Compare fees at different banks and credit unions.
  • A credit card is a loan. Unpaid balances are charged interest.
  • In a check register, add deposits and subtract payments, withdrawals and transfers out.
  • A credit report records borrowing and payments for years; a good history means lower interest.
  • Pay for college with savings, grants, scholarships, work-study and student loans. Only loans must be repaid.

Examples

Example

Balance $420. Check $135. Deposit $80.

$420 − $135 = $285

$285 + $80

Answer: $365

Example

$92,000 vs $60,000 a year for 35 years

$32,000 × 35

Answer: $1,120,000

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking a credit card is your own moneyIt is a loan; you must pay it back.
Adding a withdrawal or transfer outMoney leaving the account is subtracted.
Thinking a grant or scholarship must be repaidOnly loans are repaid.

faq.a: Checking accounts and debit cards, debit versus credit cards, check registers, credit history and credit reports, paying for college, and comparing salaries and lifetime income.

faq.q: How long does information stay on a credit report?
faq.a: Most negative information stays about 7 years; a bankruptcy can stay up to 10 years.

faq.q: What is the difference between a grant and a loan?
faq.a: A grant does not have to be paid back. A loan must be repaid, usually with interest.
Small yearly differences add up over a long career.

sets.title: Checking accounts, debit cards and credit cards

items.q: Which is a feature of a checking account?
c: It is the same as a credit report
You can never take money out
You can write checks and use a debit card to pay
items.e: A checking account is for everyday paying.

items.q: What is an overdraft?
c: Spending more than the money in your checking account
items.e: An overdraft happens when the balance goes below $0. Banks often charge a fee.

items.q: What is the main difference between a debit card and a credit card?
c: A credit card uses money in your account; a debit card borrows money
A debit card uses money in your account; a credit card borrows money you must pay back
Only a debit card can be used online
items.e: Debit = your own money. Credit = a loan from the card company.

items.q: Bank A: $5 monthly fee and $2 for each ATM use. Credit union B: $0 monthly fee and $2 for each ATM use. Lena uses an ATM 5 times a month. Which account costs less each month?
items.e: A: $5 + 5 × $2 = $15. B: $0 + 5 × $2 = $10. Credit union B costs less.

items.q: Bank A: $0 monthly fee and $2 for each ATM use. Credit union B: $5 monthly fee and $0 for each ATM use. Lena uses an ATM 3 times a month. Which account costs less each month?
items.e: A: $0 + 3 × $2 = $6. B: $5 + 3 × $0 = $5. Credit union B costs less.

items.q: What can happen if you do not pay a credit card bill in full?
c: You pay interest on the amount you still owe
items.e: Unpaid credit card balances are charged interest.

items.q: Why should you compare checking accounts at different banks?
c: Fees, minimum balances and ATM charges can be different
Only the color of the debit card is different
items.e: Banks and credit unions have different fees and rules.

items.q: Bank A: $0 monthly fee and $2 for each ATM use. Credit union B: $5 monthly fee and $2 for each ATM use. Lena uses an ATM 6 times a month. Which account costs less each month?
Bank A: $5 monthly fee and $2 for each ATM use. Credit union B: $0 monthly fee and $2 for each ATM use. Lena uses an ATM 2 times a month. Which account costs less each month?
items.e: A: $5 + 2 × $2 = $9. B: $0 + 2 × $2 = $4. Credit union B costs less.

items.q: Bank A: $4 monthly fee and $2 for each ATM use. Credit union B: $10 monthly fee and $0 for each ATM use. Lena uses an ATM 6 times a month. Which account costs less each month?
items.e: A: $4 + 6 × $2 = $16. B: $10 + 6 × $0 = $10. Credit union B costs less.

items.q: Bank A: $6 monthly fee and $2 for each ATM use. Credit union B: $2 monthly fee and $2 for each ATM use. Lena uses an ATM 6 times a month. Which account costs less each month?
items.e: A: $6 + 6 × $2 = $18. B: $2 + 6 × $2 = $14. Credit union B costs less.

items.q: Bank A: $4 monthly fee and $2 for each ATM use. Credit union B: $10 monthly fee and $2 for each ATM use. Lena uses an ATM 4 times a month. Which account costs less each month?
Bank A: $0 monthly fee and $2 for each ATM use. Credit union B: $5 monthly fee and $0 for each ATM use. Lena uses an ATM 2 times a month. Which account costs less each month?
Bank A: $0 monthly fee and $3 for each ATM use. Credit union B: $5 monthly fee and $1 for each ATM use. Lena uses an ATM 5 times a month. Which account costs less each month?
items.e: A: $0 + 5 × $3 = $15. B: $5 + 5 × $1 = $10. Credit union B costs less.

items.q: Which payment can lead to debt if you spend more than you can pay back?
c: A debit card with no overdraft
items.e: A credit card lets you borrow, which can lead to debt.

items.q: Bank A: $6 monthly fee and $3 for each ATM use. Credit union B: $2 monthly fee and $1 for each ATM use. Lena uses an ATM 2 times a month. Which account costs less each month?
items.e: A: $6 + 2 × $3 = $12. B: $2 + 2 × $1 = $4. Credit union B costs less.

items.q: Bank A: $6 monthly fee and $3 for each ATM use. Credit union B: $2 monthly fee and $1 for each ATM use. Lena uses an ATM 4 times a month. Which account costs less each month?
items.e: A: $6 + 4 × $3 = $18. B: $2 + 4 × $1 = $6. Credit union B costs less.

items.q: Bank A: $4 monthly fee and $2 for each ATM use. Credit union B: $10 monthly fee and $2 for each ATM use. Lena uses an ATM 3 times a month. Which account costs less each month?
Bank A: $0 monthly fee and $3 for each ATM use. Credit union B: $5 monthly fee and $1 for each ATM use. Lena uses an ATM 2 times a month. Which account costs less each month?
Bank A: $3 monthly fee and $3 for each ATM use. Credit union B: $8 monthly fee and $1 for each ATM use. Lena uses an ATM 6 times a month. Which account costs less each month?
items.e: A: $3 + 6 × $3 = $21. B: $8 + 6 × $1 = $14. Credit union B costs less.

items.q: Which action helps build a positive credit history?
c: Using a credit card past its limit
Paying bills on time every month

items.q: Two friends each borrow $20,000 for a car for one year. One with good credit pays 3% interest. One with poor credit pays 8%. How much more interest does the person with poor credit pay?
About how long do most late payments stay on a credit report?
items.e: Most negative information stays for about 7 years; a bankruptcy can stay up to 10 years.

items.q: Why is a positive credit history important?
c: It helps you get loans at lower interest rates
It lets you skip paying bills
items.e: Lenders trust borrowers with a good history and offer lower interest rates.

items.q: Which information is in a credit report?
c: Loans and credit cards, payment history and amounts owed
items.e: A credit report lists accounts, payments and debts.

items.q: What usually happens to someone with a poor credit history who asks for a loan?
c: They get the loan for free
They get a lower interest rate
They pay a higher interest rate or are turned down
items.e: Lenders see more risk, so they charge more interest or say no.
